Port 3000 selects Web dev server.

What the port in an address does

The host identifies a machine: localhost identifies the computer you are using, while a deployed domain identifies a publicly reachable server. It does not identify a particular service by itself.

The port identifies the service: The number after the colon directs the request to that service. If a dev server reports 3001 as occupied or switches to 3002, the browser address must change too.

What it is not

A port is not a domain name or a deployment switch. localhost:3000 is reachable only on this computer; a correct port does not make a local project public. A port conflict means two services want the same entry, not necessarily that application code failed.
